 Katie & Nathaniel — Behind the Scenes  2004-10-17

CBSA Secondary Inspection at 35 Park Street East & The U.S. Marshals File on Brandon Mercer

What Happened Between Katie and Nate's Six-Bus Escape from Williamsburg and Brandon's Arrest on Cass Avenue in Detroit

Episode 5, Chapter 1, Part 3: The Goyeau Street Tunnel Bus & The Trashed Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue ↗ All 12 Katie & Nathaniel Dossiers Copy Dossier Link:
In-Universe Date & Time 2004-10-17 • 16:15–19:40 EDT
In-Universe Location 555 Goyeau Street & 35 Park Street East, Windsor, Ontario; East Jefferson Avenue, Randolph Street, & Cass Avenue, Detroit, Michigan
From / Archival Source RaggieSoft Backstage Production Dossier
For Readers Of Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 5, Chapter 1, Parts 2 & 3)

Archival Note: In Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 5, Chapter 1, Part 2 and Part 3, readers watch nineteen-year-old twins Katie and Nathaniel Prairie take a blind leap of faith onto the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line bus outside the Williamsburg Transportation Center on Saturday, October 16, 2004—riding six buses across two transit agencies to meet their father David Prairie at Military Highway and Indian River Road at 8:01 PM—and then accompany David to the Walter E. Hoffman United States Courthouse on Granby Street in Norfolk four days later. This Backstage dossier reconstructs what happened in between from the perspective of the Williamsburg Police Department, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and the United States Marshals Service.

1. Saturday Afternoon & Night, October 16, 2004 (3:52 PM – 11:30 PM): The Blind Ticket Counter at 468 North Boundary Street

When twenty-two-year-old Brandon Mercer ordered nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate to wait outside on the brick bus loop of the Williamsburg Transportation Center while he stepped inside the historic red-brick depot, he walked up to an interior American Rail Transit System (ARTS) ticket counter with zero window line of sight to the bus bays outside.

  1. Two Full-Price, Non-Refundable Regular Adult Tickets to Detroit (DET):
    Because Brandon had never ridden public transit with disabled riders, he had no idea ARTS offered discounted Passenger with a Disability (PWD) + Companion tariffs. Instead, he emptied nearly his entire checking account (leaving $4.12 on his station ATM receipt) to pay cash for two full-price, non-refundable Regular Adult one-way rail-and-thruway tickets to Detroit, Michigan—intending to haul Katie across the river into Ontario for a "fresh start" and abandon Nate stranded on the Williamsburg platform once the train pulled in.
  2. Why Brandon Booked Detroit + Tunnel Bus Instead of Cross-Border Rail:
    Hidden inside a lockbox at the house off North Henry Street were two external hard drives containing skimmed resort front-desk credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity profiles. Afraid that booking a direct cross-border ARTS train into Ontario would transmit his name on an advance electronic passenger manifest hours before reaching the border, Brandon convinced himself that riding domestically to Detroit and walking onto a municipal Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus would let him slip quietly into Canada and sign up for free Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) coverage.
  3. Walking Out to an Empty Brick Loop (4:02 PM):
    When the manual multi-segment paper ticket jacket finished printing and Brandon pushed back out the double doors, both SwiftChair powerchairs were gone—already rolling south down Jamestown Road aboard the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line toward Lee Hall. Realizing Katie and Nate were heading straight to David Prairie and the police—and furious at the thought of eating two expensive, non-refundable Regular Adult tickets—Brandon hurried two blocks back to North Henry Street, stuffed his clothes and both contraband hard drives into a fifty-pound canvas duffel bag, and boarded the evening northbound ARTS train toward Washington, Toledo, and Detroit using his own valid Regular Adult ticket.

2. Sunday Afternoon, October 17, 2004 (3:45 PM – 4:50 PM): East Jefferson Avenue, The Tunnel Bus Farebox, & 555 Goyeau Street / 35 Park Street East

Stepping off his connecting thruway coach in downtown Detroit, Michigan on Sunday afternoon after twenty hours without sleep, Brandon walked down toward the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel plaza at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street—and made three consecutive blunders before he even reached a Canadian border podium:

  • Ripping Up Katie's Unused Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue (3:50 PM):
    Furious every time he looked at Katie's unused Regular Adult voucher inside the yellow ARTS ticket jacket, Brandon tore Katie's ticket and the attached purchase receipt in half and threw both into a municipal trash barrel on East Jefferson Avenue—unknowingly destroying the unused ticket's residual exchange value that could have paid his bus fare back to Virginia.
  • The Transit Windsor Farebox Surprise (4:00 PM):
    Boarding the cross-border Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus, Brandon discovered that Transit Windsor accepted U.S. currency strictly at a 1:1 par rate rather than giving an exchange premium, that the Canadian electronic coin validator rejected American dimes and American gold-colored one-dollar coins (because Canadian dimes use different metallic composition and Loonies have a distinct eleven-sided signature), and that municipal fareboxes issue zero change. Forced to shove his very last ten-dollar U.S. bill into the exact-fare slot to pay a single tunnel fare, Brandon rode under the Detroit River into Ontario with exactly $1.75 in American quarters left in his pocket.
  • Refusal of Entry at 555 Goyeau Street & 35 Park Street East (4:15 PM – 4:50 PM):
    Emerging onto the Canadian inspection plaza at 555 Goyeau Street (near Wyandotte Street East), all Tunnel Bus passengers were directed inside the CBSA Windsor Tunnel District Operations building at 35 Park Street East. Referred to Secondary Inspection by CBSA Officer Vance after snapping that as an American citizen with a birth certificate he had a "right" to enter Canada, Brandon had his duffel bag unpacked on the steel inspection table—revealing his birth certificate folder, $1.75 in pocket quarters, his $4.12 Williamsburg ATM slip, two external hard drives, and three pages of printed internet notes about moving permanently to Ontario and signing up for OHIP. Informed that American tourists have zero legal right to reside in Canada or receive provincial healthcare, Brandon was formally refused entry under *Sections 20 and 39 of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and—after lunging at the counter in an outburst—driven back through the tunnel in the caged rear compartment of a marked CBSA* enforcement van.

3. Sunday Evening to Tuesday (October 17–19, 2004): The CBP Contraband Seizure on Randolph Street & The U.S. Marshals Arrest on Cass Avenue

At 5:05 PM on Sunday evening, CBSA officers escorted Brandon straight through the security door of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) compound at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street in Detroit:

  1. Mandatory Warrantless Border Search (19 U.S.C. § 1582):
    Conducting a routine border examination of a foreign-refused traveler, Detroit CBP officers powered on the two external hard drives in Brandon's duffel bag—uncovering hundreds of skimmed credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity files from Williamsburg hospitality registers, instantly elevating Brandon's local misconduct into a multi-count federal wire-fraud and identity-theft prosecution.
  2. Arrested Outside the Men's Shelter on Cass Avenue (Tuesday, October 19, 2004):
    Released onto East Jefferson Avenue with $1.75 in his pocket while CBP forensic agents transmitted the seized drive images to federal prosecutors in Virginia and Michigan, Brandon walked nine blocks northwest to a brick men's homeless shelter on Cass Avenue—where Deputy United States Marshals arrested him on federal felony warrants without incident.
  3. Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) (Wednesday, October 20, 2004):
    Because the Williamsburg station security camera and ARTS ticket audit proved Katie never boarded the train and escaped six hundred miles away while Brandon destroyed her unused ticket himself on East Jefferson Avenue, Special Agent Morales at the Walter E. Hoffman U.S. Courthouse on Granby Street confirmed that Katie's name carried a permanent Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) shield—certifying zero criminal, civil, or immigration infractions in both U.S. and Canadian databases for life.
